title: CHAPTER TEN. On the simplicity of God; definition
pass_a_gloss: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): CHAPTER TEN. Concerning ye simplicity belonging toward God. And these things concerning ye second attribute belonging toward God: His third attribute follows. I. Namely simplicity, which God's highest perfection is, by which from every composition free He is. Ye vocabulary belonging toward SIMPLICITY from corporeal things we borrow. But simplicity it is called because not something positive, but chiefly ye negation belonging toward composition it notes.
pass_b_english: CHAPTER TEN. On the simplicity of God.

And these things concerning the second attribute of God: there follows His third attribute. I. Namely simplicity, which is God's highest perfection, by which He is free from every composition. The vocabulary of SIMPLICITY we borrow from corporeal things. But it is called simplicity because it notes not something positive, but chiefly the negation of composition.
source_text: CAPUT DECIMUM, De simplicitate Dei. Atque haec de secundo Dei attributo: sequitur tertium ejus attributum. I. Simplicitas videlicet, quae est summa Dei perfectio, per quam is ab omni compositione liber est. SIMPLICITATIS vocabulum a rebus corporeis mutuamur. Dicitur autem simplicitas, quia non positivum aliquid, sed negationem compositionis potissimum notat.
